LONDON and NEW YORK, 8 September, 2026 - Renalytix plc (LSE: RENX) (OTCQB: RNLXY),
a precision medicine diagnostics company focused on kidney disease,
confirms that, further to the Company's announcement released at 07:01 on 1 September 2026 (RNS Number: 8254S), a shareholder circular, containing the Notice of the General Meeting setting out the Resolutions and further details on the Fundraising, has been posted to Shareholders and is available on the Company's website at
https://investors.renalytix.com/documents/
.
The General Meeting to approve the Resolutions will be held at 12.00 p.m. on 28 September 2026 at 1 Bow Churchyard, London EC4M 9DQ.
The Circular includes a recommendation from Directors that all Shareholders of the Company vote in favour of the Resolutions, as they intend to do in respect of their own holdings of Ordinary Shares representing 5.5 per cent. of the current issued share capital of the Company.

Renalytix (LSE: RENX) (OTCQB: RNLXY) is an artificial intelligence-enabled in vitro diagnostics company dedicated to optimizing kidney disease management through precision-based care intervention. It's KidneyIntelX™ technology and data-driven insights help clinical teams understand patient level of risk for progressive decline in kidney function in the earliest stages of diabetic kidney disease. This enables clinicians to focus resources and guideline-recommended treatment, providing the best chance for improving kidney and overall renal-cardio-metabolic outcomes.
Unrecognized and uncontrolled diabetic kidney disease remains one of the largest barriers to reducing suffering and controlling cost in the United States' and the United Kingdom's medical systems, affecting approximately 15 million and 8 million people, respectively.
Renalytix has been granted FDA authorization and Medicare reimbursement for kidneyintelX.dkd which is offered commercially throughout the United States. For more information about the kidneyintelX.dkd test, visit
www.kidneyintelx.com

company_30s.what_they_do: Renalytix Plc develops and sells diagnostic tests for kidney disease, mainly the Kidneyintel™ test that helps doctors predict kidney failure earlier. It also runs a small drug pipeline focused on kidney‑related conditions and works with partners to bring its tests into clinical practice.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Kidney disease is a growing global health problem, and early detection can save lives and cut treatment costs. Renalytix sits at the intersection of diagnostics and data‑driven analytics, giving it a competitive edge over generic lab tests and a potential foothold in the expanding precision‑medicine market.
company_30s.current_state: The company is still raising capital, has a partnership with Quest Diagnostics, and is actively selling its diagnostic test to hospitals and labs. It is in a cash‑burn phase but is gaining traction through new contracts and regulatory approvals. The share price sits far below its historical highs, reflecting a steep sell‑off.

rns_narrative: Renalytix has been busy on the fundraising front: a recent AGM notice, a wrap retail offer, and a capital‑access window all point to a concerted effort to shore up liquidity. At the same time, the company is tightening its partnership network – the Quest Diagnostics collaboration and a new funding round aim to accelerate test deployment.

The company is also addressing regulatory and shareholder transparency: an AIM Rule 17 disclosure, a holdings notice, and a circular for the AGM all show it is keeping its shareholders informed. The real‑world evidence study released in June gives the test a clinical credibility boost.
Overall the narrative is one of a company pivoting from a pure‑diagnostics model to a broader, partnership‑driven growth strategy while securing the capital needed to keep the pipeline alive.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet but optimistic chatter about institutional buying
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A few traders see the new Quest deal and the capital‑access window as signs that the company is finally getting the market to believe in its test. They talk about a potential price spike once the partnership starts generating revenue.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Others caution that the company has yet to hit a sustainable revenue stream, that the capital raise could dilute shareholders, and that the test’s adoption rate remains uncertain.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The mood is shifting from silence to cautious optimism as new funding and partnership announcements surface, but the overall chatter remains muted.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – there is no public buzz, which is a good sign for a contrarian play.

near_term_catalysts: The completion of the Quest Diagnostics partnership and the first tranche of test deployments in UK hospitals could provide a revenue uptick that traders will notice.

A scheduled AGM on 8 September where the board will discuss the results of the recent fundraise and the capital‑access window could trigger a short‑term rally if the market interprets the financing as a sign of confidence.
Any regulatory approval or a positive clinical data release from the real‑world evidence study could act as a catalyst for a bounce.
expect_next.watch_for: Key signals to monitor over the next 2–3 months are: 1) a spike in trading volume that exceeds 5x the 30‑day average; 2) a price move toward the 52‑week low’s 50% recovery level; 3) a positive earnings or partnership update from Quest Diagnostics.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stages of a deep crash cycle. The APEX score (currently 9/21) indicates a tight price compression, suggesting that the next breakout could be sharp. Confirmation will come when volume surges and the price starts breaking out of the low‑range.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: Renalytix sits at the bottom of a 70‑plus‑percent crash, giving a large upside if the price recovers to halfway of its 52‑week range. A deep bottom signals a high probability of mean reversion; the partnership with Quest and the fresh capital raise add conviction. Historically, the system’s GREEN signals (average 39% return, 40% win rate) have produced solid rebounds, and a 70% drop often leads to a 2× move back to the 50% recovery level.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company is still cash‑burning and has yet to prove a repeatable revenue model. If the partnership stalls or the test fails to gain traction, the price could stay flat or decline further. A worst‑case scenario is a continued decline to the current low with no meaningful catalyst, leaving investors with a deep loss.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside: 2× or more if the price recovers to the 50% recovery level. Potential downside: a 70% drop is already in place, so the risk is capped at the current price. The asymmetry is roughly 2:1, favouring a contrarian long stance.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a breakout above the 52‑week low after a volume spike of at least 5× the 30‑day average. Size the position to risk no more than 5% of the portfolio per trade, and set a stop just below the recent support level. Take profits in stages – 50% at the 50% recovery level, the rest at the 75% recovery level.
playbook.if_watching: Hold until the AGM or the first Quest diagnostics deployment announcement. If volume surges and the price moves above the 52‑week low, consider a small entry. If the price fails to break out within 30 trading days, re‑evaluate.
playbook.if_passing: There are no imminent delisting or bankruptcy risks, so the playbook does not contain a passing scenario.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Renalytix’s steep crash, dead public sentiment and new partnership give a contrarian bullish case with a 2× upside if the price recovers to the 50% 52‑week level, while the risk is limited to the current depth of the crash.
